criteria.text: The participant has a histologically or cytologically confirmed advanced solid tumor that is positive for EGFR and has progressed despite standard therapy or for whom no standard therapy exists.
Archival tumor tissue is available for assessment of EGFR status via FDA-approved EGFR assay.
The participant is ≥ 18 years old.
The participant has at least 1 measurable lesion as defined by RECIST v1.1.
The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1.
The participant has a life expectancy ≥ 12 weeks.

Baseline organ function and laboratory data meet the following criteria: ANC ≥ 1500 cells/mm3, Platelet count ≥ 75 000 cells/mm3, Hemoglobin ≥ 8.0 g/dL, Prothrombin time ≤ 1.5× ULN, Activated partial thromboplastin time ≤ 1.5× ULN, Serum creatinine ≤ 1.5× ULN, estimated glomerular filtration rate ≥ 60 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault formula), Serum total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 mg/dL, AST and ALT ≤ 3.0× ULN (if metastases are present, ≤ 5.0× ULN).
Females are not pregnant or lactating, and females of childbearing potential and males agree to use contraception.
The participant provides written informed consent prior to any study procedures.
The participant has a history of another primary cancer ≤ 3 years, with the exception of completely resected nonmelanoma skin cancer or carcinoma in situ of uterine cervix.
The participant has active or symptomatic CNS metastases, or treated CNS metastases that have not been stable for ≥ 4 weeks or require treatment with steroids or anticonvulsants.
The participant tests positive for hepatitis C virus, hepatitis B virus, or human immunodeficiency virus infection.
The participant has active, clinically significant infections.

The participant has clinically significant cardiovascular disease, including congestive heart failure (New York Heart Association Class > 2), serious cardiac arrhythmia, myocardial infarction ≤ 6 months, or unstable angina.
The participant had a prior clinically significant allergic reaction to chimerized or murine monoclonal antibody therapy.
The participant had prior treatment ≤ 6 months with cetuximab, panitumomab, gefitinib, erlotinib, or other therapy that specifically and directly targets the EGF pathway.

The participant had anticancer therapy or investigational agents for nonmalignant disease ≤ 4 weeks or 5 half-lives, whichever is shorter, prior to Cycle 1 Day 1, with the exception of tamoxifen for patients with a history of operated breast cancer > 3 years and no evidence of disease after surgery.
The participant had major surgery ≤ 4 weeks.

The participant has a clinically significant psychiatric illness, other comorbidity, or laboratory abnormality that, in the opinion of the Investigator, makes it unsafe for the patient to participate in the study or may interfere with study compliance or study results.
The participant has other unspecified reasons that, in the opinion of the Investigator, make the patient unsuitable for enrollment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "ZZ06 in Adult Patients With Advanced Solid Tumor Malignancies". Your earlier answers already covered 5 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you 18 years of age or older?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I'm 52.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Based on your current health, do you expect to live for at least 12 weeks? It's okay if you're not sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I'm up and about and working from home. I expect to be around for a while.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be specific, do you expect to live for at least 12 weeks (about 3 months) from now? It's okay if you're not sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I expect to live at least 12 weeks. I'm up and about and working from home.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently pregnant or breastfeeding? If not, are you a female of childbearing potential or a male who agrees to use contraception during the study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm male, so no pregnancy issues. I'm not sure about the specific contraception requirements for the study.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since you are male, do you agree to use contraception during the study? It's okay if you're not sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I agree to use contraception during the study.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you willing to sign a written informed consent form before starting any study procedures?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I'm willing to sign the informed consent form. I need to understand everything before I commit.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever tested positive for hepatitis C, hepatitis B, or HIV?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I have HIV. It's undetectable on my meds for years.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for sharing that. Besides HIV, do you currently have any other active infections, such as a fever, pneumonia, or a serious bacterial infection?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any other active infections like pneumonia or a fever right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a significant heart condition, such as heart failure, a serious irregular heartbeat, a heart attack in the last 6 months, or unstable chest pain?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had a heart attack, stroke, or heart failure requiring hospital care in the last 6 months.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have a serious irregular heartbeat (arrhythmia) or unstable chest pain?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have a serious irregular heartbeat or unstable chest pain.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had a serious allergic reaction to a treatment called chimerized or murine monoclonal antibody therapy?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had a serious allergic reaction to that type of therapy.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received any treatment in the last 6 months that specifically targets the EGF pathway, such as cetuximab, panitumomab, gefitinib, or erlotinib?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had those. I had an infusion called Rybrevant, but no EGFR-targeting pills.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Just to clarify, was Rybrevant (amivantamab) the only treatment you received in the last 6 months that targets the EGF pathway? Please let me know if you're not sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, Rybrevant was the only one. I haven't had any EGFR-targeting pills like gefitinib or erlotinib.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received any anticancer treatment or investigational drug for a non-cancer condition in the last 4 weeks?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't received any anticancer treatment or investigational drug for a non-cancer condition in the last 4 weeks.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any major surgery in the last 4 weeks?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any major surgery in the last 4 weeks.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any significant mental health conditions, other serious medical issues, or abnormal lab results that might make it unsafe or difficult for you to take part in this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have any significant mental health conditions or abnormal labs that would stop me. I'm just managing my HIV and lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, do you have any serious medical conditions (like your HIV or lung cancer) or mental health conditions that might make it unsafe or difficult for you to take part in this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have lung cancer and HIV, but I'm managing both. I don't have other serious conditions that would make it unsafe to participate.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Is there anything else about your health or situation that you feel might make it difficult or unsafe for you to take part in this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't think so. I'm managing my HIV and Stage 4 lung cancer, and I'm up and about working from home. I don't have any other issues that would make it unsafe.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be sure, are there any other health issues, personal circumstances, or concerns that you feel might make it difficult or unsafe for you to take part in this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't think so. I'm managing my HIV and Stage 4 lung cancer, and I'm up and about working from home. I don't have any other issues that would make it unsafe.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
